statement: Draw a chain of straight segments from picked or typed points, with Close and Undo options, and let Enter at the first prompt continue from the end of the last line, polyline or arc.
superiority: Chain stays one undo step per pick and snaps to dimension-aware inference without a mode toggle.
notes: Verified against help page "LINE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Line, Polyline; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Script: LINE 0,0 10,0 10,5 C yields 3 lines; Continue starts at the prior endpoint; Undo removes only the last segment; endpoints exact to 1e-9.

statement: Create a 2D polyline mixing straight and arc segments, with Width, Halfwidth, Length, Undo and Close options and arc sub-options (angle, center, direction, radius, second point, endpoint).
superiority: Variable-width and bulge segments edit live with grips without exploding, and the same object converts to NURBS exactly.
notes: Verified against help page "PLINE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Polyline, Curve; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Script a polyline with 2 line and 2 arc segments and a width taper; check vertex bulges equal tan(angle/4) and widths per segment; DXF LWPOLYLINE round trip keeps all.

statement: Create a 3D polyline of straight segments only, with free Z coordinates, Undo and Close options, stored as a single object.
superiority: Edits as an ordinary curve with full 3D gumball instead of a limited vertex-only object.
notes: Verified against help page "3DPOLY (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Polyline; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Pick 4 points with different Z; object has 4 vertices, length equals sum of 3D segment lengths within 1e-9.

statement: Create a spline from fit points or control vertices (Method option, CV degree up to 10), with knot parameterization (chord, square root, uniform), tolerance, start/end tangents, close, and conversion of spline-fit polylines through the Object option.
superiority: Exact NURBS with continuity analysis and curvature graph available at creation time.
notes: Verified against help page "SPLINE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers InterpCrv, Curve; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Fit-point spline passes through all picked points within the fit tolerance; CV method degree 3 has n+4 knots; converting a smoothed pline gives a spline within 1e-6.

statement: Create circles by center with radius or diameter, 2 points, 3 points, tangent-tangent-radius, and tangent-tangent-tangent.
superiority: Tangent circles remain associative to their tangent objects when constraints are added.
notes: Verified against help page "CIRCLE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Circle; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Ttr between two lines with R=5 gives center at the expected closed-form point; 3P through unit-circle points gives radius 1 within 1e-12.

statement: Create arcs from combinations of start, second point, center, end, angle, chord length, direction and radius (three-point, start-center-end/angle/length, start-end-angle/direction/radius, center-start-end/angle/length), plus a continue-from-last-object mode, counterclockwise by default.
superiority: All 11 methods reachable from one smart arc prompt with live preview of the alternate branch.
notes: Verified against help page "ARC (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Arc; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Each of the 11 arc methods on a quarter circle of radius 10 gives sweep 90 degrees and radius 10 within 1e-9; direction of arc follows counterclockwise rule.

statement: Create ellipses and elliptical arcs from axis endpoints plus a distance or rotation, or from a center, with start/end angle or parameter modes and an included-angle option, plus an isometric Isocircle option.
superiority: Exact conic curves with direct conversion to NURBS and no 2D-only restriction.
notes: Verified against help page "ELLIPSE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Ellipse; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Axis endpoints (0,0) (10,0) with other axis 4 gives area pi*5*4 within 1e-9; elliptical arc from 0 to 90 degrees has parametric bounds correct.

statement: Draw a closed rectangular polyline from two corners, with Chamfer, Elevation, Fillet, Thickness and Width settings and Area, Dimensions and Rotation options.
superiority: Fillet and chamfer remain editable parameters after creation.
notes: Verified against help page "RECTANG (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Rectangle; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Corner (0,0) to (10,6) with fillet 1 gives perimeter 32 - 8 + 2*pi (closed form 24+2*pi); Area option with length 10 and area 60 gives width 6; Rotation applies.

statement: Create a regular closed polyline of 3 to 1024 sides defined by a center with an inscribed or circumscribed radius, or by the endpoints of one edge.
superiority: Side count and radius stay editable after creation.
notes: Verified against help page "POLYGON (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Polygon, PolygonStar; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: 6-sided inscribed in R=10 has side 10; circumscribed in R=10 has apothem 10; edge mode through (0,0)-(4,0) gives side 4.

statement: Create a filled ring made of wide arc polylines from inside and outside diameters, repeating at each picked center until Enter; an inside diameter of zero gives a filled disk.
superiority: Result can be a true planar surface with exact trim curves.
notes: Verified against help page "DONUT (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Circle, PlanarSrf; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: ID 2 OD 6 gives area pi*(9-1); ID 0 gives a filled disk of radius OD/2.

statement: Place point objects at 2D or 3D locations, with their display style and size controlled by PDMODE and PDSIZE.
superiority: Division by length or count also handles blocks aligned to curve tangent with exact arc-length parametrization.
notes: Verified against help page "POINT (Command)". Corrected: POINT page covers only point placement and the PDMODE/PDSIZE appearance; DIVIDE and MEASURE are separate commands (add separate DIVIDE row; MEASURE already has its own row). Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-2ECD656C-989D-40EE-8D1A-AF010A5CD2A2 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-3427CA9F-831C-4B53-A903-49EB6378335C Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Point, Divide; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: DIVIDE a 100-unit line into 5 gives 4 points at 20-unit spacing; MEASURE with distance 30 gives 3 points; display obeys PDMODE 35.

statement: Place point objects or blocks along a selected object at a given distance interval starting from the end nearest the pick, with an option to align blocks with the object.
superiority: Interval spacing reports leftover length and offers fit-to-ends in the same command.
notes: Verified against help page "MEASURE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Divide; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Polyline of length 100 measured at 30 gives points at 30,60,90 arc length; Block option with align rotates block to tangent.

statement: Create infinite construction lines through two points, horizontal, vertical, at an angle (optionally from a reference line), as an angle bisector, or offset from an object.
superiority: Construction lines participate in snapping and constraints but never affect zoom extents or plots.
notes: Verified against help page "XLINE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Line; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Bisect option through three points gives line along the angle bisector; Offset 5 from a line gives parallel at distance 5; extents treated as infinite for snaps.

statement: Create semi-infinite construction lines from a start point through a second point, repeating for further through points until Enter.
superiority: Rays are excluded from extents and plot by default with a clear display style.
notes: Verified against help page "RAY (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Line; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Ray from (0,0) through (1,1) intersects line x=5 at (5,5) via INTERSECT osnap.

statement: Draw a revision cloud of arcs in rectangular, polygonal or freehand form or by converting an existing closed object, with an approximate arc length, Normal/Calligraphy style, and a Modify option to replace part of an existing cloud.
superiority: Cloud arcs regenerate when the boundary is stretched and carry revision metadata.
notes: Verified against help page "REVCLOUD (Command)". Corrected: Page documents a single approximate arc chord length (min/max arc length variable is marked obsolete) and adds the Object conversion and Modify options. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers RevCloud; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Rectangle 100 by 50 with arc length 5 produces arcs with chord lengths within the min/max; Reverse flips bulge direction; area closed.

statement: Create a polygonal masking object that hides objects behind it using the background color, defined by picked points or from a polyline (with option to erase the polyline), with a Frames setting of on, off, or display-but-do-not-plot.
superiority: Mask is exact in vector PDF output instead of rasterized, and is selectable by frame in any mode.
notes: Verified against help page "WIPEOUT (Command)". | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Wipeout over a hatch hides it in plot output; Frames=off removes the border from view and from plot; DRAWORDER respected.

statement: Convert closed planar loops of lines, arcs, circles, ellipses, polylines and splines into region objects, which can then be combined by union, subtract and intersect (separate commands).
superiority: 2D region booleans return exact trimmed planar surfaces and keep parent curves for history.
notes: Verified against help page "REGION (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers PlanarSrf, BooleanUnion; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Two overlapping 10x10 squares offset by 5: union area 175, intersection 25, subtract 75 within 1e-9.

statement: Create a closed polyline or region from the area enclosed around a picked internal point, with island detection, object type and boundary set (current viewport or selected objects) options.
superiority: Gap tolerance reported and optionally auto-closed with a visible preview of the repair.
notes: Verified against help page "BOUNDARY (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-A43E133B-7F18-4F89-B559-EBFC8272595B | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry (looked for CurveBoundary, Boundary). Acceptance sketch: Pick inside a square with an inner circle: with island detection on returns two boundaries; gaps beyond tolerance fail with a clear error.

statement: Create freehand sketch geometry as lines, polylines or splines, with a configurable increment (minimum pointer travel per segment) and a fit tolerance for splines.
superiority: Freehand input is fitted by a curve with error bound shown in the prompt.
notes: Verified against help page "SKETCH (Command)". Corrected: Original described a record-style command; current help documents Type (line, polyline, spline), Increment and Tolerance options. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Record increment 1.0 over a 10-unit stroke yields at least 10 vertices; Spline type output is smooth within 0.5 increment.

statement: Create a 2D spiral or 3D helix from base and top radius or diameter, height or axis endpoint, number of turns (max 500) or turn height, and clockwise or counterclockwise twist.
superiority: Helix is an exact NURBS and feeds sweep and thread tools directly.
notes: Verified against help page "HELIX (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Helix, Spiral; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Radius 5 height 20 turns 4 has length 4*sqrt((2*pi*5)^2+5^2) within 1e-6; top radius different gives a conical helix.

statement: Draw multiple parallel lines using the current multiline style, with Justification (top, zero, bottom), Scale and Style options plus Undo and Close.
superiority: Multiline styles convert to editable offset curve sets with join logic exposed.
notes: Verified against help page "MLINE (Command)". | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Offset; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Style with 3 elements at offsets 0.5,0,-0.5 and scale 2 gives lines at +-1 and 0; closed corner joins mitered.

statement: Create, modify and manage multiline styles defining element offsets, colors and linetypes, start/end caps (line, outer arc, inner arcs, angle), background fill and joint display.
superiority: Styles are shareable between documents and imported by name.
notes: Verified against help page "MLSTYLE (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-9AE65983-DFCA-4140-889E-227B8A31D047 | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Style with 2 elements, round end cap: MLINE end shows arc cap; style round-trips through DWG.

statement: Edit multiline intersections and vertices: closed, open and merged crosses and tees, corner joints, add or delete vertex, cut single or all elements, and weld cut segments.
superiority: Junction cleanup is applied automatically and reversible.
notes: Verified against help page "MLEDIT (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-4FA12BA9-B0D5-4900-A725-EC7BD222E34B | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Two crossing MLINEs with Closed Cross remove interior elements at the crossing; Tee trims one line to the other.

statement: Draw a solid band of given width along picked points with squared ends (legacy 2D trace).
superiority: Imports as filled planar surface.
notes: REJECTED: Current help defines TRACE as the collaboration command for opening and managing feedback/markup traces (New, Open, Delete, Rename, Close); the legacy wide-line trace command is not documented. If wide solid bands are needed use PLINE with width; consider a separate row for the Trace markup feature. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Width 2 trace from (0,0) to (10,0) has 4 vertices and area 20; DXF TRACE entity preserved.

statement: Create 2D solid-filled triangles and quadrilaterals from three or four points entered in zigzag order (third point opposite the second), filled only when FILLMODE is on and the view is orthogonal, with successive points extending the solid.
superiority: Fill order is explained interactively and corrected on request.
notes: Verified against help page "SOLID (Command)". Corrected: Original described a swapped third/fourth point rule; help states the third point is opposite the second and the fourth diagonally opposite the first. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers PlanarSrf; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Points ordered 1,2,3,4 produce bow tie per rule; FILLMODE 0 hides fill; area for rectangle equals w*h.

statement: Set the point display style and size, either relative to the screen or in absolute units, stored in PDMODE and PDSIZE.
superiority: Per-viewport point style overrides.
notes: Verified against help page "PTYPE (Command)". Corrected: Current help names the command PTYPE (Point Style dialog); DDPTYPE is the legacy name and is not documented. Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-48AD2AE9-1EDE-4BF1-B3FA-F5B15225189E Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: PDMODE 3 PDSIZE -5 draws crosses 5 percent of viewport height; changing size regenerates at zoom change.

statement: Dimension and display the length of arcs and polyline arc segments (arc-length option, see also dimension section).
superiority: Arc length reported with exact tolerance in the properties panel.
notes: REJECTED: No ARCLEN command exists in AutoCAD help; arc length dimensioning is the DIMARC command (ARCLEN only appears inside variable names). Re-file under dimension domain as DIMARC. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Length; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Arc radius 10 sweep 90 gives 15.708; list shows within 1e-3.

statement: At any point prompt, let the user set a direction with the cursor and type a numeric distance to place the next point relative to the last point.
superiority: Works with units, with scale-aware inference and unit suffix typing.
notes: Verified against help page "Direct Distance Entry (Command Modifier)". | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Cursor at 30 degrees, type 12 Enter: next point at 12*(cos30,sin30) within 1e-9, in ortho and polar modes.

statement: Show tooltips near the cursor for pointer coordinates, dimension distance and angle, and command prompts, with Tab to move between fields, a lock on typed values, and a settings dialog to control each component.
superiority: Dynamic input is keyboard-accessible, screen-reader labelled and remappable.
notes: Verified against help page "About Using Dynamic Input Tooltips". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-38EC86CF-D96A-455F-A5DE-2CDA23C28FC4 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-A265C30C-CFD8-405D-BEE2-257B379475E2 | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Typing 5 Tab 30 Enter in LINE places a segment with length 5 at 30 degrees; locked fields hold when cursor moves.

statement: Accept absolute, relative (@), polar, 3D cylindrical and spherical coordinates at any point prompt, with an asterisk prefix to enter relative to the WCS, interpreted in the current UCS by default.
superiority: One unified parser with unit-aware input and error message pointing at the offending token.
notes: Verified against help page "About Coordinate Entry". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-B8CBF18A-CF79-4C0F-B0CE-73C03BE6AB53 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-184023ED-D0DA-416A-82F4-9F184F045CB9 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-8389803D-0B43-49A1-B829-0A794D3E06DD | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Line; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: @5<45 from (1,1) gives (1+3.5355,1+3.5355); *10,10 under rotated UCS gives WCS point; spherical @5<45<30 correct within 1e-9.

statement: Let the user place a point relative to a temporary reference using the FROM base-point-plus-offset modifier and the Tracking method of orthogonal offsets from a series of temporary points.

source.ref: About Specifying a Point Relative to an Existing Point

superiority: Alignment paths are visible, labelled with distances, and survive pan.
notes: Verified against help page "About Specifying a Point Relative to an Existing Point". Corrected: Page covers FROM and Tracking; the TT object snap and bare @ last-point entry are not described on it. Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-0EB8FEA1-4C14-40C6-8254-DB6693DB481C ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-528D04B1-51BB-48EF-A36B-C23619DF33D3 Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: LINE from FROM base (0,0) offset @5,5 starts at (5,5); TT with two tracked points places at the intersection of their alignment paths.

statement: Turn lines, arcs and splines into polylines and join them with other polylines, using the Multiple option with a fuzz distance to join non-touching ends and a join type of extend, add or both.
superiority: Joining reports unjoined gaps and has a visible tolerance preview.
notes: Verified against help page "PEDIT (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-648BDC21-E835-478F-A318-9D201479998D | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Join; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Three lines with end gaps 0.01 and fuzz 0.05 join to one closed polyline; Join type Add inserts bridging segments.

statement: Edit splines: fit data (add, delete, move, kink, tolerance, end tangents, purge to control vertices), control vertices (add, delete, move, weight, elevate order), close or open, join, reverse, and convert to polyline with a precision of 0 to 99.
superiority: Edit points stay visible through the edit and curvature combs update live.
notes: Verified against help page "SPLINEDIT (Command)". Corrected: Help lists no direct Knots editing option; knot parameterization is set at creation. Join, Reverse, Kink, Weight and Elevate Order are the real additional options. Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers InsertKnot, InsertControlPoint; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Add fit point at (5,5) increases fit count by 1 and the curve passes through it; Refine adds a knot without changing shape within 1e-9.

statement: Insert a table object from a table style, an empty table, or a data link, specifying column and row counts and sizes, placed by insertion point or by a window.
superiority: Cells accept formulas and live links natively.
notes: Verified against help page "TABLE (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-135907BC-6148-4DC7-93A9-65233D882919 | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Table; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Table 5 columns by 4 rows with column width 30 has width 150 and height set by row heights; cells accept text.

statement: At any point prompt, accept .x, .y, .z, .xy, .xz and .yz filters to build one point from coordinates extracted from several picks or typed values.
superiority: Filters are visible in the prompt as typed chips.
notes: Verified against help page "Coordinate Filters (Command Modifier)". Corrected: This is a command modifier available at point prompts rather than a command of its own. Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-A3F6F0F9-A085-4176-972C-8D11068E7355 Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: .X pick (3,0) then .YZ pick (0,7,2) gives (3,7,2).

statement: Change the display order of overlapping objects by moving selected objects above or under a reference object, or to the front or back of the drawing order.
superiority: Draw order stored per layout and reflected in both DWG and PDF.
notes: Verified against help page "DRAWORDER (Command)". Corrected: Command has Above, Under, Front, Back options only; text/dimension to front is TEXTTOFRONT and hatch to back is HATCHTOBACK (separate commands, hatches go to the back not the front). Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-DE1673FF-A97E-480A-8BE2-54B52F21D75C ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-F4A78D17-6BE6-4906-990C-4446268F4570 Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: Send hatch to back puts hatch behind boundary lines in plot output and in picking priority on equal depth.

statement: Bring all text, all dimensions, all leaders, or all three together in front of every other object in the drawing in a single command.
superiority: Annotation is on top by default and cannot be hidden accidentally.
notes: Verified against help page "TEXTTOFRONT (Command)". | prior app hint: no matching registration found in the cand2 app command registry. Acceptance sketch: After TEXTTOFRONT All, a wipeout above text is below text in display order.

statement: Temporarily hide everything except selected objects (ISOLATEOBJECTS) or hide only selected objects (HIDEOBJECTS), and restore them with UNISOLATEOBJECTS, without changing layers.
superiority: Isolation is a lightweight view state shown with a persistent chip.
notes: Verified against help page "ISOLATEOBJECTS (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-48199A62-90B6-48C6-93E1-5ECF56EAF8B5 ; https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-B21B3F6C-7F67-465A-A97E-5E8ADC87B6D4 | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Isolate, Hide, Show; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: ISOLATEOBJECTS hides unselected; UNISOLATEOBJECTS restores; object isolation state not saved in layer table.

statement: Remove unreferenced named items (blocks, layers, linetypes, text and dimension styles, groups, materials) and also zero-length geometry, blank text and obsolete leftover data, with optional nested purging.
superiority: Shows an exact reference-count report per item before removal.
notes: Verified against help page "PURGE (Command)". Corrected: Help lists the named items above; shapes and multiline styles are not named on the pages read. Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-C6B62BBD-C363-4DC7-AF43-036A7B287473 Acceptance sketch predates this review and was not re-checked. | prior app hint: cand2 app registers Purge; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Purge All removes an unreferenced block definition and an empty layer but keeps in-use layers and the current layer.

statement: Remove duplicate and overlapping lines, arcs and polylines, and combine partially overlapping or end-to-end collinear objects, with a numeric tolerance and a choice of object properties to ignore.
superiority: Runs on the whole drawing with a diff preview and exact tolerance bound.
notes: Verified against help page "OVERKILL (Command)". Also see: https://help.autodesk.com/view/ACD/2025/ENU/?guid=GUID-A9927B3C-7C30-43FB-B6A9-29843B35001C | prior app hint: cand2 app registers SelDup; behavior and option coverage not verified against this row. Acceptance sketch: Two coincident lines reduce to one; two overlapping collinear lines with partial overlap combine to one; tolerance 0.001 respected.

statement: The program must create three- or four-sided planar or nonplanar faces in 3D space from successive corner points, continuing with further faces from the last two points, and support marking individual edges invisible.
notes: Added from help page "3DFACE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run 3DFACE with four points, then press Enter and enter two more points; two adjacent 3D faces exist sharing an edge, and entering I before an edge's first point makes that edge invisible.

statement: The program must create a legacy polygon mesh by prompting for M and N sizes between 2 and 256 and then a vertex location for every (m,n) position row by row, producing an open mesh in both directions.
notes: Added from help page "3DMESH (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run 3DMESH with M=3 and N=4 and supply 12 vertices; one polygon mesh with 3 by 4 vertices that is open in both directions is created.

statement: The program must provide a command-line -BOUNDARY that creates a region or polyline from an enclosed area given an internal point, with options for boundary set, island detection and object type, where PLINETYPE controls the polyline kind.
notes: Added from help page "-BOUNDARY (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw four lines forming a closed rectangle, run -BOUNDARY choosing Polyline and an internal point; assert a closed polyline with four vertices is created, and with Object Type Region assert a region is created.

statement: The program must place point objects or block references at equal intervals along a single curve-type object (line, polyline, arc, circle, ellipse, spline), with the Block option optionally aligning blocks to the object tangent.
notes: Added from help page "DIVIDE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: DIVIDE a 100-unit line into 5 segments and assert 4 points at X=20,40,60,80; repeat with a block and Align Yes on an arc and assert the block X axes are tangent.

statement: The program must draw double lines from straight and arc segments with Break, Caps (Both, End, None, Start, Auto), Dragline offset and Snap options, as documented for AutoCAD LT.
notes: Added from help page "DLINE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DLINE across an existing line with Break on and assert the crossing line is split at the double line edges and end caps are placed per the Caps setting.

statement: The program must measure distance, radius, angle, area and volume interactively, including a Quick mode that dynamically reports dimensions and enclosed-area values as the cursor moves and supports cumulative area with multiple selections.
notes: Added from help page "MEASUREGEOM (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run MEASUREGEOM Distance between (0,0) and (3,4) and confirm 5; run Area with a 2x2 square's corners and confirm area 4 and perimeter 8.

statement: The program must provide SHAPE to insert a shape from a loaded SHX shape file by name at a given insertion point, height and rotation.
notes: Added from help page "SHAPE (Command)"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Load a shape file, run SHAPE with a named shape at the origin with height 2, and assert a shape object with that name and size is created.

statement: MEASURE and DIVIDE must place points or blocks along polylines, lines, arcs, splines, circles and ellipses, either at fixed distances or dividing the object into a chosen number of equal segments, without breaking the object apart.

source.ref: About Specifying Equal Intervals on Objects

notes: Added from help page "About Specifying Equal Intervals on Objects"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: DIVIDE a 100-unit line into 4 segments and assert three points at 25, 50 and 75 are created and the line remains one object.

statement: Line objects must be created as individually editable segments with layer, linetype and lineweight, with precise point entry via object snaps, tracking, grid snap and direct distance.
notes: Added from help page "About Lines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a two-segment line sequence with endpoint snap and assert two separate LINE entities with coincident shared endpoint exist.

statement: Polylines must be single objects joining line and arc segments, supporting constant or tapered widths, unit-level move and copy, continuous linetype generation across vertices, and rectangle and polygon creation.
notes: Added from help page "About Polylines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a polyline with one line and one arc segment of width 2, move it and assert a single object with intact vertices and widths.

statement: Multilines must be drawn from styles of parallel elements with selectable justification and scale (scale not affecting linetype scale).
notes: Added from help page "About Multilines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Draw a STANDARD multiline with scale 2 and top justification and assert two parallel elements offset by 2 units and aligned to the cursor path per justification.

statement: SKETCH must record freehand input as small segments controlled by SKETCHINC and convert the result into lines, polylines or splines according to SKPOLY and SKTOLERANCE.
notes: Added from help page "About Freehand Sketches"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Sketch a stroke with SKPOLY=1 and assert one polyline is produced whose segment length does not exceed SKETCHINC.

statement: Reference (construction) geometry such as lines, circles, points, xlines and rays must be creatable and preservable to guide creation and checking of other objects.
notes: Added from help page "About Reference Geometry"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create an xline and a ray through a point, snap a new line to their intersection and assert the endpoint coincides.

statement: Curved objects, including splines, ellipses, donuts, polyline arcs, circles and arcs, must be creatable through their documented methods, such as three-point arcs, and circles by center and radius, two points, three points or tangent-tangent-radius.
notes: Added from help page "About Curved Objects"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a circle with the tangent-tangent-radius option between two lines and assert it is tangent to both with the given radius.

statement: Dino 8 must create arcs from combinations of three points, start/center/end, start/center/angle, start/center/length, radius, direction and similar inputs, counterclockwise by default and clockwise when Ctrl is held while dragging.
notes: Added from help page "About Arcs"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run ARC with the 3-point method on points (0,0),(5,5),(10,0) and assert a counterclockwise-or-clockwise arc through all three; run Start,Center,Angle with center (0,0), start (10,0), angle 90 and assert a CCW arc ending at (0,10).

statement: Dino 8 must create circles by center and radius or diameter, by 2 or 3 points on the circumference, and tangent to two or three objects with a given radius or via Tangent object snaps.
notes: Added from help page "About Circles"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run CIRCLE center (0,0) radius 5 and assert radius 5; run CIRCLE TTR on two perpendicular lines with radius 2 and assert the circle is tangent to both lines.

statement: Dino 8 must create donuts as closed wide polylines defined by inside and outside diameters and a center, repeating for further centers, with an inside diameter of 0 producing a solid-filled disc.
notes: Added from help page "About Donuts"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run DONUT with inside 2, outside 4, center (0,0) and assert a closed polyline of width 1; with inside 0 assert a solid-filled circle of diameter 4.

statement: Dino 8 must create ellipses from major and minor axes (axis endpoints plus a distance), including isometric circles when drawing on isometric planes.
notes: Added from help page "About Ellipses"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run ELLIPSE with axis endpoints (0,0) and (10,0) and a second-axis distance of 3 and assert major radius 5 and minor radius 3 centered at (5,0).

statement: Dino 8 must create and edit cubic NURBS splines through fit points or from control vertices, with a grip that toggles between displaying fit points and control vertices.
notes: Added from help page "About Splines"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create a spline through four fit points and assert it passes through each; switch the grip to control-vertex display and assert the control polygon is shown.

statement: Dino 8 must create helixes (open 2D or 3D spirals approximated by splines) from base radius, top radius, height, turns, turn height and twist direction, producing a cylindrical helix when radii are equal, conical when they differ and a flat spiral at height 0.
notes: Added from help page "About Helixes"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Run HELIX with base radius 5, top radius 5, height 10 and 4 turns and assert a cylindrical helix of 4 turns; run again with height 0 and assert a planar spiral; assert entering 0 for both radii is rejected.

statement: Dino 8 must create regions as 2D enclosed areas with mass properties from closed loops of linear, curved and spline segments, and combine them with union, subtract and intersect.
notes: Added from help page "About Regions"; statement written from the opening part of that page (about the first 1,300 to 1,500 characters), so options further down the page were not reviewed. Acceptance sketch: Create two overlapping circles as regions, run UNION and assert one region whose area equals the combined area minus the overlap; SUBTRACT and INTERSECT give the corresponding areas.
